trial_title: Standard Radiation Therapy With or Without Stereotactic Radiation Therapy in Treating Patients With Glioma
brief_summary:
RATIONALE: Radiation therapy uses high-energy x-rays to damage tumor cells and may be an effective treatment for patients with glioma. Stereotactic radiation therapy may be able to deliver x-rays directly to the tumor and cause less damage to normal tissue. It is not yet known if standard radiation therapy is more effective when followed by stereotactic radiation therapy.

PURPOSE: Randomized phase III trial to compare the effectiveness of standard radiation therapy with or without stereotactic

eligibility_table.criterion: Histologically proven WHO grade III or IV glioma at primary diagnosis that enhance on preoperative imaging Glioblastoma Anaplastic astrocytoma Gliosarcoma Tumor volume no greater than 4.0 cm in maximum diameter on preoperative CT or MRI No prior histology of WHO grade I or II glioma Astrocytoma Oligodendroglioma No brainstem or infratentorial tumor No multifocal glioma Safe to treat tumor stereotactically No close proximity to critical structures, e.g., optic chiasm
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has anaplastic astrocytoma of the spine, which is a WHO grade III glioma, but the tumor is unresectable and there is no information on tumor volume or proximity to critical structures.

eligibility_table.criterion: No prior malignancies within 5 years except nonmelanomatous skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of anaplastic astrocytoma, which is a malignancy within the last 5 years.

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any prior chemotherapy treatments, including temozolomide, CPT-11, or Avastin, before the current trial?
Has the patient received any adjuvant chemotherapy concurrently with radiation therapy in the past 30 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: No prior radiotherapy to the head and neck area
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any prior radiotherapy to the head and neck area?

eligibility_table.criterion: No prior radiotherapy to the brain
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any prior radiotherapy to the brain?

eligibility_table.criterion: No more than 6 weeks since other prior radiotherapy
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has undergone prior radiotherapy, and there is no indication that it has been more than 6 weeks since the last treatment.

eligibility_table.criterion: Able to tolerate full course of conventional radiotherapy
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's severe lower extremity weakness and urinary retention may indicate an inability to tolerate a full course of conventional radiotherapy.

eligibility_table.criterion: No prior or concurrent medical condition that would preclude study therapy
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has multiple medical conditions, including chronic pain and hypertension, which may preclude study therapy.
The patient's history of severe lower extremity weakness suggests a performance status lower than WHO 0 or 1.
